อุโบสถและเจดีย์เป็นโบราณสถานที่ยังใช้งาน: The ordination hall and pagoda are active historical sites, and the temple serves as the first provincial meditation practice center of Phang Nga. The Fine Arts Department (Krom Sinlapakon) announced its registration as a historical site and defined its land boundaries in the Royal Gazette on December 18, 1996 (2539 BE).
ชมอาคารก่ออิฐถือปูน หน้าบันและซุ้มประตูห: Observe the brick and mortar building, with its pediment and arched doors and windows decorated with stucco, including Buddha images and floral patterns. It is one of the important historical sites within the temple and is still in an active temple. The temple is located on the west bank of Khlong Takua Pa, with the canal situated to the east of the temple.

วัดนิกรวราราม หรือวัดย่านยาว เริ่มสร้างใ: Wat Nikon Wararam, or Wat Yan Yao, was initially built in 1793 (2336 BE) by Khun Ta Kaew and Khun Ta Ram. The discovered evidence verifies the year and the names of the founders, but does not provide detailed reasons on what specific mission the temple was established for. Therefore, it should be viewed as a religious site of the local community forming in the Takua Pa basin, rather than tying it to stories without direct evidence.
เมืองตะกั่วป่าในภาพกว้างมีประวัติเป็นเมื: The broader picture of Takua Pa town has a history as a port town and tin mining source, with maritime trade and various groups of people. However, no temple-specific evidence has been found to verify the role of Wat Nikon Wararam regarding tin mines, maritime trade, Hokkien Chinese people, or the governor system. Thus, no conclusions are made beyond the data sources.
วัดได้รับพระราชทานวิสุงคามสีมาใน พ.ศ. 23: The temple received the royal granting of the land for a temple in 1842 (2385 BE), which is a crucial piece of evidence that the religious site was certified as an area for monastic activities according to the Sangha's tradition at the time. However, no documents have been found specifying major restorations, changes in ownership, or periods of abandonment.
หลังสึนามิวันที่ 26 ธันวาคม 2547 วัดถูกใ: After the tsunami on December 26, 2004 (2547 BE), the temple was used as a gathering place for the bodies of disaster victims awaiting forensic identification. This temporary role made Wat Yan Yao a part of Takua Pa's disaster response history. Later, on October 30, 2022 (2565 BE), the Samnakngan Phraphutthasatsana Changwat Phangnga (Phang Nga Provincial Office of Buddhism) participated in handing over the land title deed document to the abbot, serving as evidence of land ownership management in the modern era.

หลักฐานล่าสุดที่ค้นพบยืนยันว่า วัดยังใช้: The latest discovered evidence verifies that the temple is still in use, with Phra Khru Nikon Thammasophit as the abbot, and has monks in residence during the Buddhist Lent. The temple database indicates the organization of the united Kathina ceremony in 2024 (2567 BE) and 2025 (2568 BE), while government/local news verifies the temple's participation in district and provincial level activities.
ในช่วงไม่กี่ปีที่ผ่านมา วัดเป็นทั้งพื้นท: In recent years, the temple has been both a space for religious activities and a public space: in 2024 (2567 BE) it was used as a donation center to help northern flood victims, and there was an inspection visit for the Temple, People, State, Creating Happiness project as a southern regional model temple. However, no data has been found verifying the opening and closing hours for tourists, detailed building conditions, or temple-specific restoration projects in 2026 (2569 BE).
